claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMC RNA from seven Ad5-seronegative vaccinees after primary vaccination (day 0) at 24 h postvaccination (day 1), 72 h postvaccination (day 3), and 168 h postvaccination (day 7) showed a broad innate transcriptional response peaking at day 1 with 1,026 genes enhanced and 1,048 repressed, waning by day 3 and returning to baseline by day 7 compared to prevaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: Responses to MRKAd5/HIV peaked at 24 h, with 1,026 genes exhibiting enhanced and 1,048 genes exhibiting repressed expression levels compared with prevaccination (Fig. 1A and Dataset S1, tab 1). At 72 h postvaccination, the differentially expressed genes were a small subset of those detected at 24 h (Dataset S1, tab 2). No significantly differentially expressed genes were detected at 168 h.

claim_2.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMC RNA from seven Ad5-seronegative vaccinees after primary vaccination (day 0) validated increased expression of module-associated genes including CXCL10, ISG-15, and STAT1 at 24 h postvaccination (day 1) compared to prevaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: First, we quantified and confirmed the differential expression of mRNAs associated with several vaccine-regulated modules, including “Interferon response” [C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10), ISG-15, and STAT1] (Fig. 1C).

claim_3.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from vaccinated subjects showed robust increases in IP-10, I-TAC, MCP-1, MCP-2, IL-10, and IL-1Ra at 24 h postvaccination (day 1) compared to prevaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: Next, we corroborated the differential expression of many cytokines and chemokines at the protein level using multiplex serum analyte analysis (Fig. 1D and Dataset S1, tab 6), detecting robust changes in serum levels of IP-10, I-TAC, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and MCP-2, as well as immunoregulatory IL-10 and IL-1Ra.

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of whole blood from vaccinated subjects after primary vaccination (day 0) showed vaccine-induced influx of monocytes and pronounced efflux of lymphocyte populations including T, B, and NK cells at 24 h postvaccination (day 1) compared to prevaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: Finally, we validated the cellular trafficking responses predicted from the modular analysis by directly assessing circulating peripheral blood leukocyte concentrations (Fig. 1E and Dataset S1, tab 7), confirming vaccine-induced influx of monocytes and pronounced efflux of lymphocyte populations (T, B, and NK cells).

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMC RNA from separate donors stimulated in vitro with MRKAd5 showed that 8 of 13 modules induced in vivo were also induced in vitro, including the three interferon response modules, and 92% concordance for induction of IFN response genes between in vivo and in vitro.

sources.quote: We found that 8 of 13 (62%) modules induced in vivo were also induced in vitro and these consisted of the three “Interferon response modules” as well as unannotated modules largely comprised of innate immune response genes (Fig. 2A). Remarkably, 92% concordance between the in vivo and in vitro induction of IFN response genes was observed (Dataset S1, tab 8).

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMC RNA showed that preexisting Ad5 neutralizing antibodies attenuated MRKAd5/HIV-induced innate immune responses in vivo, with 306 seropositivity effect genes identified and critical innate immune pathways including complement pathways, innate immune sensors, and G-protein coupled receptor signaling significantly attenuated in subjects with Ad5 nAb >200 compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb ≤200.

sources.quote: Given the possibility of threshold effects of Ad5 nAb (3, 4), we compared the responses between subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤ 200 and >200, and thereby identified 306 seropositivity effect genes (302 at 24 h, six at 72 h) for which the vaccine-induced responses were markedly attenuated (Dataset S1, tab 11). Canonical pathway enrichment analysis of these genes revealed that induction of complement pathways, innate immune sensors, and G-protein coupled receptor signaling was significantly attenuated (Dataset S1, tab 12).

claim_7.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from vaccinated subjects showed that cytokine responses were markedly attenuated in subjects with Ad5 nAb >200 compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb ≤200, including lower IP-10/CXCL10 concentrations at 24 h postvaccination (day 1).

sources.quote: Finally, we validated these transcriptional results at the protein level by analyzing serum analytes from a larger set of vaccinated subjects (Fig. S2). Consistent with the transcriptional results, cytokine responses were markedly attenuated in Ad5 nAb >200 subjects compared with Ad5 nAb ≤ 200 subjects (Fig. 3C and Dataset S1, tab 13).

claim_8.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from 31 vaccine recipients at 24 h postvaccination (day 1) showed that MCP-1 and MCP-2 discriminated subjects with detectable or high Gag-specific CD8+ T-cell responses from CD8neg subjects, indicating higher chemokine induction predicted increased likelihood of positive CD8+ T-cell responses.

sources.quote: Two chemokines, MCP-1 and MCP-2 (Fig. S4 A and B), discriminated between CD8mod/CD8high subjects and CD8neg subjects with high accuracy (81% and 88%, respectively), and thus were qualitatively predictive of the vaccine CD8+ T-cell immunogenicity. In both cases, higher chemokine induction predicted increased likelihood of positive CD8+ T-cell responses.

claim_9.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMC RNA from 31 vaccine recipients showed that 209 genes induced at 72 h postvaccination (day 3) were positively or negatively associated with the magnitude of MRKAd5/HIV-induced CD8+ T-cell responses, and only 88 positively associated and 121 negatively associated genes differed significantly between high and low responders.

sources.quote: Based on the frequency of Gag-specific CD8+ T-cell responses detected at day 28 after immunization (Fig. S3), we categorized vaccine recipients (n = 31) into high, moderate, or low responders.

Surprisingly, significant differences between these groups of subjects were only identified from the transcriptional responses measured at 72 h postvaccination (88 genes were positively associated and 121 genes were negatively associated) (Fig. 5A and B and Dataset S1, tab 14)

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMC RNA comparing MRKAd5/HIV and YF-17D showed that MRKAd5/HIV induced more than 1,000 genes and repressed a similar number at 24 h postvaccination (day 1), whereas YF-17D induced only 181 genes and repressed 10 genes, indicating a broader but more transient response for MRKAd5/HIV.

sources.quote: Although the MRKAd5/HIV vaccine induced more than 1,000 genes and repressed a similar number, the YF-17D vaccine only induced 181 genes and repressed 10 genes (Fig. 6A). However, the response to MRKAd5/HIV was rapid and transient, but the response to YF-17D lagged and was persistent (Fig. 6A).
